function.name: weather_forecast_get
function.description: Retrieve the current weather forecast for a specific location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location you want to retrieve the weather for.

hour.description: The hour of the day in 24-hour format (optional). If not provided, the current hour will be used. Default: 24

message.content:
I don’t have access to live clocks here, so I’ll show you how you can figure out the current time in New York yourself:

| Step | What to do |
|------|------------|
| **1** | Find your own computer’s current Coordinated Universal Time (UTC). On most systems you can type something like `date -u` (Linux/macOS) or look up “current UTC” online. |
| **2** | Determine whether Daylight Saving Time (DST) is in effect in New York. In 2026, DST starts on the second Sunday in March and ends on the first Sunday in November. Since today is May 13, DST *is* in effect. |
| **3** | Subtract four hours from UTC to get Eastern Daylight Time (EDT), because New York is UTC‑04:00 when DST is observed. |

So, if your UTC clock reads e.g., **17:30**, then subtract 4 hours → **13:30** (or 1:30 PM) in New York.

If you’re looking for a quick way without doing calculations, many world‑clock widgets or websites let you search “New York time” and they automatically adjust for DST.
